label: copy-phase input c (copying the letter c back, from the 3rd copy step on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is the letter c (that is, original token t-L-1 was c). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and never on any other input token. Rate is near zero at recall_idx 1 (c fed back right after <DEL>, i.e. the first token was c), so the predicate requires recall_idx >= 2. Missed activations (0.5% of mass) are all weak ones from that early case. About 11% of predicted steps are inactive. The strongest activations in the examples appear when c is copied in the middle of a longer sequence. Magnitude does not track next_out == c (a cc pair), which covers only about 2% of mass.

issues: The claims check out. On the test split the predicate scores P 0.886, R 0.980, F1 0.931 and mass recall 0.994, matching the report. The profile shows the feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and in_tok == c accounts for 100% of activation mass.
recall_idx == 1 (c fed back right after <DEL>) holds 0.5% of mass at an active rate of 0.003, so excluding it is justified. Test misses come from this case and are weak (around 0.01-0.19 of max).

There is a small sub-pattern among the false positives: when c follows another c (prev_tok == c, the second c of a cc pair), precision drops to 0.55. That subset is only about 2% of predicted steps and 1% of mass. Excluding it does not improve F1 (test F1 0.928 vs 0.931).

The other false positives (about 10%) look scattered. Precision is somewhat lower when c appears more than once in the original sequence (0.82 vs 0.92) and at recall_idx == 2 (0.78), but neither gives a better predicate.

The 'magnitude does not depend on next output c' claim holds: the next_out == c subset has mass_recall/recall of about 1.0 (0.024/0.024), even though many of the top examples happen to be the first c of a cc pair. The 'stronger in the middle' claim is supported: for recall_idx >= 3 and to_go >= 2, precision is 0.95 and mass share is above count share (0.47 vs 0.39).
Minor wording: 'from the 3rd copy step on' means recall_idx >= 2, i.e. the second fed-back token. The label could say 'from the second fed-back token onward'.
